# PM036: cycle-overdue

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| family | PM |
| product | frob |
| severity (default) | warn |
| tier | universal |
| scope | repo |
| fix | manual |
| polarity | P+ |
| must_measure | false |
| version | 1 |
| since | 2.0.0 |

An active cycle is past its end date and has not been closed.

Fires once per overdue cycle, naming it and the days overdue. While it
stands, `frob work` and `frob start` refuse standard tickets with
`E-PM-CYCLE-OVERDUE` (an expedite ticket still starts).

## Remedy

Close the cycle with `frob cycle close --retro TEXT`, which carries the
incomplete work to the next cycle and records the retro.

## Examples

### PM036 active cycle past its end date / An active cycle that ended yesterday fires naming the cycle and the days #1 (line 10) (fire)

```text
cycle a start=-8 end=-1
```

### PM036 active cycle past its end date / An active cycle that ends today is not overdue #2 (line 16) (clean)

```text
cycle a start=-6 end=0
```

### PM036 active cycle past its end date / An active cycle still running is clean #3 (line 22) (clean)

```text
cycle a start=-2 end=5
```

### PM036 active cycle past its end date / A closed cycle past its end is clean #4 (line 28) (clean)

```text
cycle a start=-10 end=-3 closed
```

### PM036 active cycle past its end date / A planned cycle in the future is clean #5 (line 34) (clean)

```text
cycle a start=3 end=10
```

### PM036 active cycle past its end date / Each overdue cycle fires, a current one beside it does not #6 (line 40) (fire)

```text
cycle a start=-20 end=-14
cycle b start=-13 end=-6
cycle c start=-5 end=2
```
